scenes.line2: How do you spot schema drift?
scenes.say: When your data structure shifts, what happens to your pipeline? How do you catch schema drift before it causes trouble?

scenes.label: Drift
scenes.sub: Schema drift is when source data structure changes unexpectedly.
scenes.say: Schema drift means the shape of your source data changes without warning. Columns might be added or removed, breaking downstream steps.
To detect drift, monitor schema versions, alert when something changes, and quickly coordinate updates with upstream teams.

scenes.title: Schema drift alert
scenes.say: If a new column appears in the orders table, your transformation might fail. An alert goes out so you can fix it fast.

scenes.question: What’s your first step after drift?
scenes.right: Check the schema change, alert the team, and update transformations as needed.
scenes.say: Interviewers may ask what you do when schema drift happens. Don’t just rerun the pipeline—investigate, alert, and adapt your transformations.
